subject: Deployment mode & EU data residency \u2014 follow-up from call
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Sofie Berg <sofie.berg@nordbank.com>, Lukas Andersen <lukas.andersen@nordbank.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-01T09:12:00Z
Subject: Deployment mode & EU data residency — follow-up from call

Hi Sofie / Lukas —

Thanks again for your time this morning. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery: we covered your high-level goals (secure, low-latency customer-facing LLM features for customer support automation) and the main constraint: where PII must be processed and stored.

Options we discussed (short):
- Hosted API: fast onboarding, EU-region tenancy (data at rest + processing in EU regions we operate), shared infra.
- Dedicated capacity: single-tenant GPU pools reserved for your org (hosted by Redwood in EU regions), better isolation and predictable throughput.
- Private VPC / on-prem: customer-managed VPC or on-prem deployment for strict regulatory controls (customer KMS, direct network controls).

What we need from you to recommend the right path:
1) Confirm whether PII must remain in the EU for both processing and storage (yes/no), and whether non-PII can leave the region.
2) Any specific country requirements (e.g., Norway/Sweden vs general EU) or banking regulator expectations?
3) Priority ranking: speed to production vs absolute data residency/isolation vs cost.

Attachments: SOC2-report-2026.pdf (attached) and a short data residency FAQ I can follow up with.

Proposed next steps:
- If EU-only processing + storage is sufficient, we can scope Hosted API in EU regions or Dedicated capacity.
- If you require customer-managed infrastructure or local cloud tenancy (e.g., an Oslo/Stockholm region inside your cloud account), Private VPC is the right path — we can bring a technical runbook.
- I can book a 60min technical deep-dive with our infra lead (Aditya) next week — please share availability.

Would you prefer a short technical session (60m) or a pricing + MOPs call first?

Thanks,
Lauren

Senior AE, Redwood Inference

From: Sofie Berg <sofie.berg@nordbank.com>

Date: 2027-06-01T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Deployment mode & EU data residency — follow-up from call

Hi Lauren / Aditya —

Thanks for the recap — that aligns with our notes. A few clarifications from our side:
- Yes: PII (customer names, account numbers, transaction metadata) must be processed and stored within the EU; that is a hard requirement from our legal/compliance team.
- Non-PII telemetry (anonymized usage metrics) can be processed outside the EU if needed.
- We have strict expectations for auditability and KMS control for production systems.
- Ideally, we'd like the hosting to be within either Ireland, Frankfurt, or an availability zone in Scandinavia (Oslo/Stockholm) — regulators are specific about cross-border flows in some cases.

Question: if Redwood provides Hosted API with EU regions, does that guarantee that all PII stays in EU (both processing and rest)? Or do we need a Private VPC to satisfy our auditors? Also want to understand if Dedicated capacity can be isolated enough to meet auditors without a Private VPC.

Procurement (cc'd) will also need a preliminary ballpark for both Dedicated and Private options to assess budget.

Thanks,
Sofie Berg
Head of Cloud Security, Nordbank
sofie.berg@nordbank.com

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Sofie Berg <sofie.berg@nordbank.com>, Lukas Andersen <lukas.andersen@nordbank.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, procurement@nordbank.com
Date: 2027-06-01T13:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Deployment mode & EU data residency — follow-up from call

Hi Sofie / Lukas —

Great questions — I made notes and pulled in Aditya to confirm specifics on region availability and compliance implications. Summary below (high-level):

1) Hosted API (EU regions):
- We operate Hosted API endpoints with data residency in EU regions (currently Ireland (eu-west-1) and Frankfurt (eu-central-1)). For requests routed to these regions, both processing and default persisted logs/outputs remain in-region.
- That said, Hosted API is a multi-tenant offering. For banks with strict auditor expectations around tenancy and KMS controls, Hosted API alone sometimes does not satisfy the "customer-managed key" requirement.

2) Dedicated capacity (Reserved):
- Dedicated pools are single-tenant at the organizational level (reserved GPU clusters hosted in an EU region). Data stays in the region, and we provide tenant-level separation and audit logs. Dedicated typically satisfies stronger isolation requirements while keeping Redwood managing the infra.
- We can integrate with your cloud KMS in some Dedicated configurations (we should validate with Aditya).

3) Private VPC / On-prem:
- This is the strongest control: customer-managed VPC or on-prem deployment where you control the network and KMS. Recommended when auditors require the customer to maintain the keys or when local tenancy is mandated (e.g., bank must run within a customer-owned cloud project in a specific country).

Region availability note (short):
- We do not currently run a Redwood-managed region inside customer-owned Oslo/Stockholm cloud projects by default, but Private VPC deployments in those locations are possible (we have runbooks for partner cloud regions and on-prem). Hosted/Dedicated can run in our Ireland/Frankfurt regions; if a regulator insists on a Norway-hosted instance inside your cloud account, that points to Private VPC.

Next suggested steps:
- If EU-only residency + Redwood-managed infra is acceptable, let's evaluate Dedicated capacity first (good middle ground).
- If your auditors demand customer-managed keys or local tenancy, we'll scope Private VPC and share a runbook and effort estimate.

Aditya: can you confirm feasibility of KMS integration for Dedicated and an estimated lead time for a Private VPC in Norway/Sweden?

I've attached our data-residency FAQ for a quick read (data-residency-faq.docx). Happy to jump on a technical 60m session next week — propose Tue/Wed/Thu mornings (CEST).

Best,
Lauren
